messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: storing a dataframe
parts:
Oh, that won't work at all. Try this instead:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  values <- reactiveValues(a=NULL)
  observe({
    values$a <- make.a.vector.or.dataframe.bases.on.wigdet.inputs()
  })
})

However, are you sure you don't want to just do it like this?

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  # Define the vector or dataframe or whatever as a reactive expression
  myVector <- reactive({
    make.a.vector.or.dataframe.bases.on.wigdet.inputs()
  })

  # Use the reactive expression as if it's a function
  output$vectorPlot <- renderPlot({
    print(qplot(data=myVector(), ...))
  })
})

myVector will only be recalculated once each time the inputs change, even if you make many calls to it from your different renderXXX functions or other reactive expressions.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: storing a dataframe
parts:
I sort-of understand what you are doing now. A couple of pointers:
  1. If no file is selected, make.eval.table() raises an error, and thus an error occurs in observe({}). Apparently, in Shiny, if an error happens in an unprotected observer, the session ends. I'm not currently sure whether to categorize this as a feature or bug, but I'm leaning toward feature, as we have no idea what you intended in the observer and whether it is critical to the app.

    You have a couple of approaches you can use to deal with this. The one more commonly espoused on this list is to detect the conditions where an error might occur, and have your reactive expressions return NULL. For example, you read input$file$datafile in a bunch of reactive expressions, without checking if a file is even selected. If you change these all to check for NULL first, and return NULL immediately, the app no longer errors. I made these changes and the app seems to stop crashing; if you can't figure out the changes for yourself let me know and I'll try to send you a patch file.

    In your case, you have a LOT of reactive expressions, and many outputs as well; you may want to consider the second approach which is to catch the error at the observer/render methods (i.e. try() or tryCatch()). It depends on how you want to approach the problem I guess.

  2. Avoid the use of periods in input/output IDs. This may cause problems on the JavaScript side, since periods are not allowed in JavaScript identifiers.

Am Freitag, 31. Mai 2013 08:17:31 UTC+2 schrieb Joe Cheng [RStudio]:
I sort-of understand what you are doing now. A couple of pointers:
  1. If no file is selected, make.eval.table() raises an error, and thus an error occurs in observe({}). Apparently, in Shiny, if an error happens in an unprotected observer, the session ends. I'm not currently sure whether to categorize this as a feature or bug, but I'm leaning toward feature, as we have no idea what you intended in the observer and whether it is critical to the app.

    You have a couple of approaches you can use to deal with this. The one more commonly espoused on this list is to detect the conditions where an error might occur, and have your reactive expressions return NULL. For example, you read input$file$datafile in a bunch of reactive expressions, without checking if a file is even selected. If you change these all to check for NULL first, and return NULL immediately, the app no longer errors. I made these changes and the app seems to stop crashing; if you can't figure out the changes for yourself let me know and I'll try to send you a patch file.

    In your case, you have a LOT of reactive expressions, and many outputs as well; you may want to consider the second approach which is to catch the error at the observer/render methods (i.e. try() or tryCatch()). It depends on how you want to approach the problem I guess.

  2. Avoid the use of periods in input/output IDs. This may cause problems on the JavaScript side, since periods are not allowed in JavaScript identifiers.

Am Mittwoch, 1. Mai 2013 06:24:24 UTC+2 schrieb Joe Cheng [RStudio]:
Oh, that won't work at all. Try this instead:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  values <- reactiveValues(a=NULL)
  observe({
    values$a <- make.a.vector.or.dataframe.bases.on.wigdet.inputs()
  })
})

However, are you sure you don't want to just do it like this?

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  # Define the vector or dataframe or whatever as a reactive expression
  myVector <- reactive({
    make.a.vector.or.dataframe.bases.on.wigdet.inputs()
  })

  # Use the reactive expression as if it's a function
  output$vectorPlot <- renderPlot({
    print(qplot(data=myVector(), ...))
  })
})

myVector will only be recalculated once each time the inputs change, even if you make many calls to it from your different renderXXX functions or other reactive expressions.
